title: Suppression Of Coherent Light Scattering In A Three-dimensional Atomic Array
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: Experiments with a three-dimensional atomic array demonstrate strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering.
motivation: Previous studies on collective light scattering in atomic arrays focused on one- and two-dimensional systems; extending to three dimensions is crucial for understanding and controlling light-matter interactions in more realistic geometries.
method: The authors experimentally realize a three-dimensional atomic array and measure the suppression of coherent scattering in all directions.
result: They observe strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering, indicating collective effects unique to three-dimensional arrays.
conclusion: This work opens new avenues for controlling light propagation and quantum nonlinear optics using three-dimensional atomic arrays, with potential applications in quantum information processing and simulation.

title: Hong–Ou–Mandel Interference Of More Than Ten Indistinguishable Atoms
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstration of Hong–Ou–Mandel interference with up to 12 indistinguishable atoms, showing a clear multiparticle interference pattern.
motivation: Extend HOM interference from photons to massive particles and from few to many particles, testing quantum indistinguishability and multiparticle interference.
method: Experimental setup with ultracold neutral atoms, single-atom resolution, and negligible loss; measurement of interference patterns for ensembles of up to 12 atoms.
result: Observed characteristic multiparticle HOM interference pattern with up to 12 atoms, confirming indistinguishability and quantum interference at a larger scale.
conclusion: Opens new possibilities for quantum metrology and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics with massive particles; may impact quantum information processing.

title: Single- And Two-mode Magnon Thermal Squeezing
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of thermal squeezing of magnons in a ferrimagnetic insulator, achieving noise below thermal levels.
motivation: To realize squeezed states in magnets for enhanced spin-based sensing and information technology.
method: Thermal squeezing of magnons in a ferrimagnetic insulator device, likely using nonlinear interactions or parametric processes.
result: Demonstrated that magnon noise can drop below thermal levels, indicating squeezed states.
conclusion: This work opens avenues for quantum-enhanced magnonics and spin-based technologies, with potential applications in sensing and information processing.

title: Scaling Matters Of Cell Fate
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports a universal scaling law in DNA methylation dynamics during early embryo development, suggesting physical constraints govern cell fate.
motivation: To understand whether cell differentiation is driven by molecular specifics or universal physical principles.
method: Analysis of methylation dynamics in early embryos, likely using high-throughput sequencing and scaling analysis.
result: Methylation dynamics follow a universal scaling law, independent of molecular details.
conclusion: Physical constraints may shape cell fate, implying a fundamental principle in developmental biology.

title: Decoupling Adhesion From Jamming In Phase Transitions Drives Tissue Organization
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how adhesion and jamming phase transitions drive tissue organization in cellular collectives, using in silico and in vivo experiments.
motivation: To understand how multiple control parameters, specifically cell density and adhesion, influence phase transitions and material states in tissues, and how these transitions direct developmental programs.
method: The authors independently tuned cell density and adhesion in both computational models (in silico) and living organisms (in vivo) to observe their effects on tissue material state and organization.
result: Adhesion dictates the tissue material state; adhesion-driven solidification in unjammed pluripotent tissues drives epithelial organization, revealing that phase transitions direct developmental programmes.
conclusion: The findings uncover a mechanism where adhesion controls tissue material properties and organization, with implications for developmental biology and tissue engineering.

title: Thorium-229 Lifetime Locked Down
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 May 2026;
tldr: The paper resolves a decade-long puzzle about the anomalously short lifetime of a nuclear metastable state in thorium-229 ions, revealing an uncommon decay channel.
motivation: The lifetime of the nuclear metastable state in singly charged thorium-229 ions appeared shorter than theoretical predictions, puzzling physicists for about ten years.
method: The study likely involved experimental measurements of the decay rate and theoretical modeling to identify the decay channel.
result: The solution provides evidence for an uncommon decay channel that explains the observed shorter lifetime.
conclusion: The findings resolve a long-standing discrepancy and may have implications for nuclear clocks and fundamental physics.

title: Evidence For The Generic Existence Of Two Local Structures In Liquid Water
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: Simulations suggest the existence of two interconvertible local structures in liquid water, supporting the two-state picture of deeply undercooled water.
motivation: To provide evidence for the long-predicted two-state regime in deeply undercooled water by identifying two distinct local structures.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of liquid water.
result: Two local structures that undergo interconvertible reactions were identified, corroborating the two-state picture.
conclusion: The findings support the two-state model of water and may have implications for understanding water's anomalous properties.

title: Adhesion-driven Rigidity Transition Decoupled From Density-driven Jamming Triggers Epithelial Organization In Embryonic Tissues
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies adhesion-driven rigidity transitions in embryonic tissues, unrelated to quantum information or condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand how epithelial organization emerges during morphogenesis, specifically the role of adhesion versus density in tissue rigidification.
method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of embryonic tissues, likely using biophysical measurements and modeling.
result: Adhesion-driven rigidification is key to epithelial organization and is decoupled from density-driven jamming.
conclusion: Provides new insight into phase transitions in biological tissues, with implications for developmental biology.
